author: Scalix World
description: Official Scalix Cloud MCP server and plugin — 53 platform tools over one remote endpoint: PostgreSQL, serverless functions, AI inference, storage, computers, KV, DNS, events. https://scalix.world/mcp
name: Scalix Cloud MCP

resources.name: Database Schema
resources.description: Full database schema as structured JSON

tools.description: Get the relationship map showing how tables are connected via foreign keys.
tools.name: scalix_db_relationships

tools.description: Search for columns by name or type across all tables.

query.description: Search term to match column names or types

tools.name: scalix_db_search_columns

tools.description: List all columns classified as containing personally identifiable information (PII).
tools.name: scalix_db_pii

tools.description: Analyze a SQL query and return optimization suggestions including index recommendations and query rewrites.

sql.description: SQL query to analyze and optimize

tools.name: scalix_db_optimize

tools.description: Translate a plain-language question into a candidate SQL query using pattern-matching against the live schema (no AI model — simple questions only: counts, averages, filtered selects on a named table). Returns the SQL without executing it, with a confidence score; low confidence means the table was guessed. Review the statement and tables_used, then run it with scalix_db_query. For complex questions, read scalix_db_schema and write the SQL directly.

question.description: The question to answer from the database, in plain language (e.g. 'how many orders shipped last week?')

tools.name: scalix_db_text_to_sql

tools.description: Execute a SQL query against the project database. Returns columns, rows, row count, and cost breakdown. Destructive statements (DROP/TRUNCATE/bulk DELETE) require a two-step confirmation: the first call returns code CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED with a confirmation_token — re-call with that value in confirm_token to execute.

confirm_token.description: Confirmation token from a prior CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED response; required to execute destructive SQL (single-use, short TTL)

timeline_id.description: F17: run the query against a BRANCH timeline of this project instead of the primary. Takes the timeline_id returned by scalix_db_branch_create (or its db_<timeline_id> form). A timeline that is not a branch of this project fails the call — it never falls back to the primary. Omit for the primary.

tools.name: scalix_db_query

tools.description: Get the full database schema including all tables, columns, types, and relationships.
tools.name: scalix_db_schema

tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific database table including columns, indexes, and foreign keys.
tools.name: scalix_db_table

tools.description: Apply a database migration by version number.
tools.name: scalix_db_migrate

tools.description: List storage buckets, or list objects in a specific bucket with optional prefix filter.

bucket.description: Bucket name (aliases: name). If omitted, lists all buckets.

name.description: Alias of bucket — accepted for symmetry with create/delete

tools.name: scalix_storage_list

tools.description: Upload content to object storage. Provide the content as a base64-encoded string.

name.description: Alias of bucket — accepted for symmetry with create/delete

tools.name: scalix_storage_upload

tools.description: Download an object from storage. Returns the content as base64.

name.description: Alias of bucket — accepted for symmetry with create/delete

tools.name: scalix_storage_download

tools.description: Create a new Scalix Storage bucket in the project (S3-compatible object storage). Bucket names must be unique within the project. Setting public=true makes every object in the bucket readable without authentication — leave it false (the default) and use presigned URLs for private sharing. Public buckets double as static websites: upload index.html and serve it from the project's store subdomain at https://{slug}.store.scalix.world/buckets/{bucket}/objects/ (directory requests serve index.html; a 404.html object is served as the error page).

bucket.description: Alias of name — accepted for symmetry with the object tools

name.description: Bucket name, unique within the project (aliases: bucket)

public.description: true = all objects publicly readable without auth (also serves as a static website on {slug}.store.scalix.world); false (default) = private, share via presigned URLs

tools.name: scalix_storage_create_bucket

tools.description: Permanently delete an object (key) from a storage bucket. Irreversible.
tools.name: scalix_storage_delete_object

tools.description: Permanently delete a storage bucket and every object in it. Irreversible.
tools.name: scalix_storage_delete_bucket

tools.description: List all deployed serverless functions.
tools.name: scalix_fn_list

tools.description: Deploy a Scalix Function — serverless, per-request billed, running in isolated microVMs — from a container image. Invoke it with scalix_fn_invoke once deployed.

region.description: Canonical region id to deploy into (from GET /v1/regions). Omit to use the organization's recorded region preference.

region_pinned.description: true = hard-pin placement to `region`: the deploy fails closed when that region has no capacity instead of placing elsewhere. Requires `region`.

runtime.description: Runtime — `node` or `python` (exactly what the functions orchestrator accepts)

tools.name: scalix_fn_deploy

tools.description: Invoke a deployed function with a JSON payload.

data.description: JSON payload to pass to the function

tools.name: scalix_fn_invoke

tools.description: Read a single value from the project's key-value store by exact key. Returns the stored value, or a not-found error if the key does not exist or its TTL has expired. Use scalix_kv_list to discover keys by prefix first.
tools.name: scalix_kv_get

tools.description: Set a key-value pair with optional TTL.
tools.name: scalix_kv_set

tools.description: List keys in the key-value store, optionally filtered by prefix.
tools.name: scalix_kv_list

tools.description: Run AI inference on Scalix AI. Sends a prompt and returns the model's response in the OpenAI-compatible chat-completions format; tokens are billed to the project's credit pool. Discover available model IDs with scalix_ai_models.

model.description: Model ID (from scalix_ai_models — a scalix-auto/* tier or a scalix-gw/<vendor>/<model> catalog id)

tools.name: scalix_ai_infer

tools.description: List the AI models available to the project — virtual tiers and the pass-through catalog model IDs — for use in scalix_ai_infer.
tools.name: scalix_ai_models

tools.description: Publish an event to a topic. Provide an event_type (a short name for the kind of event, e.g. 'user.created') and the data payload.
tools.name: scalix_events_publish

tools.description: List the event-bus topics in the project, with each topic's ID and name. Use this to find or verify a topic_id before publishing with scalix_events_publish; publishing to a non-existent topic fails.
tools.name: scalix_events_topics

tools.description: Create a cron schedule to run a function or webhook on a timer.
tools.name: scalix_cron_create

tools.description: Execute code in an isolated sandbox. Supports Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Bash. Returns stdout/stderr, the probed interpreter version, and any files the code wrote (base64, under size/count caps).
tools.name: scalix_sandbox_run

tools.description: Get or create a persistent Linux machine by name. Idempotent — calling it again with the same name returns the existing machine rather than creating another, so it is safe to retry. Unlike a sandbox, the disk survives stop/start and is only erased by scalix_computer_delete.

disk_gb.description: Root disk in GB, 5-200 (default 10). Fixed at create — disks do not grow. Ignored if the machine already exists.

memory_mb.description: Memory in MB, 512-32768 (default 1024). Ignored if the machine already exists.

name.description: Machine name: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, max 63 characters. Unique to you.

region.description: Optional canonical region id (from GET /v1/regions) to place the machine in. Ignored if the machine already exists — a Computer is host-bound for life. Omit to let the platform pick.

ssh_keys.description: OpenSSH public keys to authorise for root, max 32, e.g. ["ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3Nz… you@laptop"]. Only needed if a human will ssh in — exec, write_file and read_file all work without one. Send the public half only; a private key is rejected. Ignored if the machine already exists — use scalix_computer_set_ssh_keys to change them. Supplying this needs the sandbox:execute scope on top of sandbox:create, because a key is a root shell; omit it and sandbox:create alone is enough.

vcpus.description: vCPUs, 1-16 (default 1). Ignored if the machine already exists.

tools.name: scalix_computer_create

tools.description: Replace the ssh keys authorised for root on a persistent Linux machine. This is how you revoke: send the list without the key you want gone, and on a running machine it stops working immediately. Sending an empty list removes every key. Not a patch — whatever you send becomes the whole list, so read the current keys from scalix_computer_list first if you mean to add one.

ssh_keys.description: The complete list of OpenSSH public keys, max 32. Empty array removes all of them.

tools.name: scalix_computer_set_ssh_keys

tools.description: List your persistent Linux machines with their status, address and resource shape.
tools.name: scalix_computer_list

tools.description: Run a command inside a persistent Linux machine and wait for it to finish. Returns exit code, stdout and stderr. The machine must be running.

args.description: Arguments passed to the program; omit when command is a shell string

command.description: Either a bare program (e.g. bash, with args passed separately) OR a full shell string (e.g. "apt-get install -y jq") — a command containing whitespace is run via sh -lc automatically, so no manual ["-lc", ...] wrapping is needed

env.description: Environment variables for this command only

id.description: Machine id from scalix_computer_create or scalix_computer_list

timeout_ms.description: Give up after this many milliseconds, 1000-300000 (default 120000). 300s is the platform-wide hop ceiling — a larger request is served at 300s, not rejected.

tools.name: scalix_computer_exec

tools.description: Write a text file into a persistent Linux machine. Use this instead of shelling out with cat/echo — no quoting to get wrong.

mode.description: Unix mode in decimal, e.g. 493 for 0755. Omit unless the file must be executable.

path.description: Absolute path inside the machine, e.g. /root/app/main.py

tools.name: scalix_computer_write_file

tools.description: Read a text file out of a persistent Linux machine.
tools.name: scalix_computer_read_file

tools.description: Stop a persistent Linux machine. The disk and the network address are kept, so starting it again returns the same files at the same address. Stop machines you are done with — a stopped machine costs only its disk.
tools.name: scalix_computer_stop

tools.description: Start a stopped persistent Linux machine. Same disk, same address.
tools.name: scalix_computer_start

tools.description: Permanently delete a persistent Linux machine AND its disk. This cannot be undone — use scalix_computer_stop if you may want the files back.
tools.name: scalix_computer_delete

tools.description: List your crews with their ids and names. A crew is a team of AI members that share a notice board; use the crew id with the board tools.
tools.name: scalix_crew_list

tools.description: Read a crew's notice board: every pinned note plus the newest unpinned ones, current as of this call. The board is the crew's shared coordination state — read it before starting work so you act on the latest news, and post what teammates need to know with scalix_crew_board_post.
tools.name: scalix_crew_board_read

tools.description: Post a note to the crew's notice board for other members and the human to see. The board is news, not knowledge: set ttl_seconds so routine updates expire on their own, pin only what every future task must see, and set owner_member_id to hand work off to a specific member. Notes cannot be edited from here — post a correction instead.

author_member_id.description: Your member id, so the note is attributed. Omit when posting as the human.

body.description: The note, max 8000 chars. Write for a teammate who was not watching your work.

owner_member_id.description: Hand off: the member id now responsible for this item.

pinned.description: Keep this in front of everyone indefinitely. Default false; most notes should expire instead.

recipient_member_id.description: Address the note to one member — a direct message that still rides the shared board.

ttl_seconds.description: Seconds until the note expires, 60 to 7776000 (90 days). Omit for no expiry — usually only right for pins.

tools.name: scalix_crew_board_post

tools.description: Add a custom domain to the project. Returns DNS records to configure.
tools.name: scalix_domain_add

tools.description: List all custom domains and their SSL/verification status.
tools.name: scalix_domain_list

tools.description: Verify DNS configuration for a custom domain and provision SSL certificate.
tools.name: scalix_domain_verify

tools.description: Create a new container image build from a Git repository or Dockerfile.
tools.name: scalix_build_create

tools.description: Get the status and logs of a build.
tools.name: scalix_build_status

tools.description: Create a new project within an organization. Returns the project ID, name, and slug. Issue an API key for the new project separately. Needs an admin API key: organization admin scope is never delegated to a connected app, so this tool fails on an OAuth connection.
tools.name: scalix_project_create

tools.description: List every project in an organization, with each project's ID, name, and slug. Use this to resolve a project ID before calling project-scoped tools. `org_id` is optional: omit it to list the projects of the organization the API key belongs to (resolved via GET /v1/me). Needs an admin API key: organization admin scope is never delegated to a connected app, so this tool fails on an OAuth connection.

org_id.description: Organization ID whose projects to list. Optional — defaults to the API key's own organization.

tools.name: scalix_project_list

tools.description: Configure end-user authentication for the project — require MFA, require email confirmation, and set the allowed auth providers. Needs an admin API key: organization admin scope is never delegated to a connected app, so this tool fails on an OAuth connection.

require_email_confirmation.description: Require users to confirm their email before a session is issued

tools.name: scalix_auth_configure

tools.description: Get the current health status of the Scalix Cloud platform including all service components.
tools.name: scalix_status

tools.description: Deploy a long-running container service on Scalix Run from a container image. Creates a new service, or a new revision of an existing service with the same name, with health checks, a public HTTPS URL, and autoscaling between min_instances and max_instances (min 0 = scale-to-zero when idle). Billed per vCPU-hour while instances run. Roll back a bad revision with scalix_run_rollback.

image.description: Container image from the Scalix registry ({registry}/{project_id}/{repo}:{tag}). External registries (Docker Hub, etc.) are NOT supported — build & push first with scalix_build_create.

region.description: Canonical region id to deploy into (from GET /v1/regions). Omit to use the organization's recorded region preference.

region_pinned.description: true = hard-pin placement (initial AND scale-out replicas) to `region`: the deploy fails closed when that region has no capacity instead of placing elsewhere. Requires `region`.

tools.name: scalix_run_deploy

tools.description: List all deployed container services in the project.
tools.name: scalix_run_list

tools.description: Change the autoscaling bounds of an existing Scalix Run service without redeploying it. Raising min_instances keeps instances warm (no cold starts, higher cost); min_instances 0 enables scale-to-zero when idle. Takes effect immediately. Find service IDs with scalix_run_list.

max_instances.description: New maximum instance count the service may scale up to

min_instances.description: New minimum instance count (0 = scale-to-zero when idle)

tools.name: scalix_run_scale

tools.description: Roll a Scalix Run service back to an earlier revision — omit 'revision' to return to the immediately previous one. Traffic switches to the target revision; the replaced revision is kept and can be redeployed later. Use scalix_run_list to see services and their current revisions.

revision.description: Revision number to roll back to; omit for the immediately previous revision

tools.name: scalix_run_rollback

tools.description: Permanently delete a Scalix Run service. This cannot be undone: it stops the running instances, releases the public HTTPS URL, erases any attached volumes and discards every revision, so scalix_run_rollback cannot bring it back afterwards. To stop paying for an idle service without losing it, set min_instances to 0 with scalix_run_scale instead.
tools.name: scalix_run_delete
